text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The caretaker government plans to increase wheat import target for 1996/97 (July-June) to 2.3 million tonnes from 1.8 million due to shortfall in wheat production.
- The Privatisation Commission has been reconstituted by raising its membership to 12 to ensure transparency and early disinvestment of larger state-owned units.
- Pakistan Sugar Mills Association has demanded imposition of excise duty on dark brown sugar lumps called gur.
- The government has constituted a special committee on formulation of macro economic framework up to the year 2001 to review and formulate new strategy for the development planning.
- Chief Election Commissioner Fakhre Alam has said army troops would be granted extraordinary powers to maintain law and order during February 3 polls.
- Provincial Ombudsman Justice (retired) Mohammad Munir Khan was gunned down by two unidentified assailants a few hundred yards away from his residence in Punjab province capital Lahore.
- Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves have improved to more than $700 million with the receipt of $150 million loan from the United Arab Emirates.
- The country was facing economic crisis and there could be more taxes to overcome this situation, said caretaker prime minister Meraj Khalid.

- Interior Minister Omar Khan Afridi has said that mainstream political leaders in the country including Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto will not be arrested to allow them to run their election campaigns freely.
- Due to strike of oil tankers, the prices of vegetable ghee have shot up to 50 rupees per kg.
Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto has said that President Farooq Leghari was a bank defaulter but had managed to get his name removed from the defaulters list. -- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
